title: U.S. House · California's 22nd Congressional District
area: Kern, Tulare, and Kings counties in the southern San Joaquin Valley, including Delano, Wasco, and parts of Bakersfield.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 elections under Proposition 50, a mid-decade redistricting measure voters approved in a November 2025 special election. Ballotpedia identifies the new 22nd District as more Democratic-leaning than the pre-2026 lines, and rates the general election a battleground contest.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, David Valadao won 40.7% of the vote (32,491 votes) and Randy Villegas won 32.4% (25,808 votes), narrowly beating fellow Democrat Jasmeet Bains (26.9%, 21,458 votes) to advance.
As of June 30, 2026, Valadao had raised $4.93 million and Villegas had raised $2.65 million, according to Ballotpedia's summary of campaign-finance disclosures.

candidates.name: David Valadao
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2013, with a 2019–2021 gap after losing re-election in 2018)

summary.text: David Valadao is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for California's 22nd District. A Hanford dairy farmer and the son of Portuguese immigrants, he served in the California Assembly before his first election to Congress in 2012; he lost in 2018 and won the seat back in 2020. His campaign website says he will focus on water, costs, jobs and job training, and benefits for seniors and veterans.

background.text: Born April 14, 1977, and raised in Hanford, California, where his family, who emigrated from the Azores Islands of Portugal in 1969, started a dairy farm in 1973. According to his House biography, the family business now includes two dairies and more than 1,000 acres of farmland in Kings County.
Graduated from Hanford High School in 1995 and attended College of the Sequoias in Visalia.

Worked on his family's dairy farm and served as Regional Leadership Council Chairman for Land O'Lakes Inc.; his House biography says he has held leadership roles in dairy organizations and cooperatives.
Elected to the California State Assembly (30th District) in 2010 and served from 2010 to 2012, including as Vice-Chair of the Agriculture Committee.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2012 to represent California's 21st District and served from 2013 to 2019. He lost the 2018 election to TJ Cox and returned to the House after winning the 2020 election.

Represents California's 22nd District after redistricting; in the 2025-2026 Congress he sits on the House Appropriations Committee, where he chairs the Legislative Branch Subcommittee and also serves on the Defense and Agriculture subcommittees. His House biography says he has served on Appropriations throughout his time in Congress.
According to his House biography, he has focused on agriculture and water policy affecting the Central Valley. He and his wife Terra, whom he married in 1999, have three children, the biography says.
His campaign website says he will 'protect our water, put an end to out-of-control inflation and outrageous gas prices, work to bring new jobs and job training to the Central Valley.'

priorities.text: Congress must provide robust support for our social safety-net programs, like Medicare and Medicaid so they can continue to ensure access to health care for all Americans.
I firmly believe we must increase our supply of safe, clean energy to provide power for our electrical grid.
I believe in a simpler and fairer tax code that puts more money back in the pockets of working families and individuals across the Valley.

positions.summary: Opposes expanding government-run health coverage, saying the Affordable Care Act restricted care and that health care decisions should stay with patients and doctors rather than the government.
positions.quote: It is my priority to ensure your health care remains in the hands of you and your doctor, not the government.

record.text: Chairs the House Appropriations Subcommittee on the Legislative Branch and serves on its Defense and Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration subcommittees in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Randy Villegas
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 32.4% of the vote, narrowly ahead of fellow Democrat Jasmeet Bains (26.9%)

summary.text: Randy Villegas is the Democratic nominee for California's 22nd District. A Bakersfield native and the son of immigrants, he is a political science professor at College of the Sequoias and a Visalia Unified School District trustee, and previously worked as a journalist and community organizer. He is running on Medicare for All, workers' rights and a pledge not to take corporate PAC money, according to his Ballotpedia survey.

background.text: Born and raised in Kern County, California, in a working-class family; the son of immigrants, he says he grew up in Bakersfield and attended Golden Valley High School. He co-owns his family's auto shop, according to a KGET interview.

Earned an associate degree in political science from Bakersfield College (2015), a bachelor's degree in political science from CSU Bakersfield (2017), and a master's degree and a Ph.D. in Politics (with an emphasis in Latin American and Latino Studies) from UC Santa Cruz (Ph.D. 2022).

Before graduate school he worked as a journalist and community organizer in Bakersfield, and has written articles and opinion pieces for outlets including the Los Angeles Times and the Bakersfield Californian.

Teaches political science at College of the Sequoias in Visalia, where he was an associate professor as of 2021; he received the American Political Science Association's 2025 Community College Faculty Award.

Provisionally appointed to the Visalia Unified School District Board (Trustee Area 6) in December 2021 and elected to the seat in November 2022. He says he has won pay increases for teachers and staff.

Has served on the boards of the nonprofits Power California and Alisal Community Arts Network and as a volunteer drumline instructor at a local high school, according to the district's 2021 announcement.

Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary. Endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, Dolores Huerta, the California Nurses Association, the California Teachers Association, the United Auto Workers, Latino Victory Fund, and the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

priorities.text: Names healthcare as his top priority, saying he will fight for Medicare for All, negotiate prescription-drug prices, and cap insulin costs at $35.
Supports passing the PRO Act to strengthen labor organizing rights and investing federal dollars in job training and small businesses in the Central Valley.
Opposes what he calls 'endless tariff trade wars' that he says hurt Valley farmers and businesses.

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All and federal negotiation of prescription-drug prices, including capping insulin at $35.
positions.quote: In Congress I'll fight for Medicare for All, take on big Pharma by negotiating the price of prescription drugs directly, bringing down costs like making insulin $35 for everyone.

positions.summary: Opposes broad tariff trade wars, saying they hurt Central Valley farmers and businesses.
Supports the PRO Act to strengthen workers' ability to organize for better wages, benefits, and working conditions.
